summary.headline: Medi Assist Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 20.3% and retention down to 90.2%.
summary.overview: Operating revenue grew 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore and group revenue grew 25.5%, while operating EBITDA rose 14.3% to INR48 crore at a 20.3% margin. Reported PAT was INR27.6 crore, or INR24.5 crore excluding a one-time INR3.1 crore derivative gain. Retention fell to 90.2% in the quarter, which management attributed to Paramount book transition, portfolio rationalisation and a high base. Management also announced the separation of Chairman and CEO roles, with Dr. Chhatwal moving to Non-Executive Chairman subject to AGM approval on 8 September.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating revenue (revenue from contracts, excl. other income)

financial_highlights.change: Includes one-time INR3.1 crore derivative gain; normative PAT INR24.5 crore

segments.name: Group TPA
segments.commentary: Revenue INR166 crore, up 25.5% YoY, with group market share at 37.6%. Same-store growth averaged about 7-8%, slower in large IT companies and faster elsewhere.

segments.name: Retail TPA
segments.commentary: Retail TPA-model revenue INR23.4 crore, up 13.1% YoY. Management says platform-administered retail premiums reached over INR4,254 crore, about 29% market share, versus INR521 crore TPA-model premiums.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28.5 crore, up 35.3% YoY, now across 16 states; management called it margin accretive and said it serves over 31 crore members across 12 states and 4 UTs under TPA model.

segments.name: International (Mayfair)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR10.1 crore, down 5.2% YoY, hit by softness in student, leisure and marine volumes. Ownership raised to 91.75%; first technology contract went live in Thailand from 1 July 2026.

segments.name: Technology SaaS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.8 crore, up 55.5% YoY, 3.3% of consolidated revenue. Fraud savings from MAven Guard exceeded INR183 crore in Q1; 7 insurers contracted across MAven, MAtrix and Magnum stacks.

guidance_outlook: Complete the Paramount integration: over 95% of group claims and over 80% of retail claims were on MAtrix at Q1 end, with the balance targeted for Q2 FY27.
Management expects Paramount-related retention drag to normalise through FY27 and EBITDA margin to return towards the pre-integration 22-23% level by the end of FY27.
Management says group and retail will grow at par with or faster than the market; government growth is opportunistic.
Management expects technology and international to become meaningful contributors to growth and EBITDA margin over time, funded from operating cash flows.
capex_capacity: Company spent about INR24.5 crore on its AI stack over the last six quarters under a Board-approved roadmap, funded from operating cash flows.
Platform processed over 186,000 pre-authorisations within 5 minutes in Q1; Raksha Prime delivered zero-wait discharge for over 87,000 members across 6,000 hospitals.
demand_pricing: Retention at 90.2% in Q1, below the historical 93-94%, due to onboarding challenges with a large acquired book, portfolio rationalisation and a higher base.
Management says its PSU group premium growth of 28.9% compares with industry PSU group premiums down about 1.5%, while overall group health industry growth was about 14%.
DSO improved 4.5 percentage points versus the prior-year trend for the quarter, on a higher receivables base.
Revenue per average headcount on non-government contracts was INR13.2 lakh annualised.
Management said international Q1 is not representative, citing softness in student, leisure and marine volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How should retail business trajectory be interpreted, given the traditional TPA model looks plateaued while technology grows fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TPA-model retail line is reported narrowly, so it should be viewed alongside platform and technology revenue, which together indicate market-share gains. Platform-administered retail premiums are over INR4,254 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin recovery to 23%, and is FY27 likely to be a record profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the immediate priority is finishing Paramount integration and returning to the 22-23% margin band towards the end of FY27. It did not give a FY27 profit target and does not break out margins by line of business.

qa_highlights.question: Does government business strain working capital, and should revenue from it be capped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government collections are the safest as they come from state and central governments, and it is margin accretive. Consolidated DSOs include government and are improving.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic growth of the legacy group TPA book, and what is the outcome-based contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is about 90%, same-store growth is about 7-8%, and new business seasonality distorts quarterly figures. It declined to give the outcome-based contract details beyond saying it is tied to fraud, waste and abuse outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of PSU TPA in-housing (HITPA) shifting premiums away from Medi Assist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not comment on specific TPAs, that the policyholder-choice regulation supports it, and that its share of wallet has improved in both PSU and private group.

qa_highlights.question: What is NPS Swasthya and what is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is the health benefit administrator and technology platform connecting NPS members, CRAs, pension funds, insurers and networks, and that it is at an early stage with potential platform and incremental TPA revenue.

risks_watch: Group retention at 90.2% versus the historical 93-94%; management did not disclose a breakdown of the retention figure.
Paramount integration completion and the target to move the remaining claims to the MAtrix stack in Q2 FY27.
PSU in-housing (HITPA) trend could shift group premiums away from the company.
International revenue fell 5.2% YoY; student, leisure and marine volumes are soft.
Management did not provide a separate depreciation breakdown; this was deferred offline.
key_quotes: And we expect this near-term PHS retention drag will get fully normalized through FY27.
So it's a true reflection of the generic capabilities of the pl atforms we have built and is an indication of the work that we can do in markets outside India.
It's a little hard for us to break that out today.
Yes, that is true. I mean our share of wallet has improved. In fact, in both the segments, both in PSU and private, our share of wallet has improved, yes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the technology platform, the NPS Swasthya scheme and the 95%+ MAtrix migration for group claims, with management repeatedly tying a return to the 22-23% margin band to FY27 end. Cautious or evasive on the causes and size of the 90.2% retention, declining to break it out, and on group TPA organic growth, depreciation and the outcome-based contract details.
